original_value: The dietary habits of people directly impact their health conditions. Especially in elder populations (in 2017, 6.7% of the world’s population was over 65 years of age), these habits could lead to important-nutrient losses that could seriously affect their cognitive and functional state. Recently, a great research effort has been devoted to using different technologies and proposing different techniques for monitoring food-intake. Nevertheless, these techniques are usually generic but make use of the most innovative technologies and methodologies to obtain the best possible monitoring results. However, a large percentage of elderly people live in depopulated rural areas (in Spain, 28.1% of the elderly population lives in this type of area) with a fragile cultural and socioeconomic context. The use of these techniques in these environments is crucial to improving this group’s quality of life (and even reducing their healthcare expenses). At the same time, it is especially challenging since they have very specific and strict requirements regarding the use and application of technology. In this Systematic Literature Review (SLR), we analyze the most important proposed technologies and techniques in order to identify whether they can be applied in this context and if they can be used to improve the quality of life of this fragile collective. In this SLR, we have analyzed 326 papers. From those, 29 proposals have been completely analyzed, taking into account the characteristics and requirements of this population.

result.paraphrase: Dietary habits have a direct effect on people’s health. In older adults, this is especially significant: in 2017, 6.7% of the world’s population was over 65, and poor diets can cause losses of essential nutrients that may seriously impair cognitive and functional abilities. Much recent research has focused on monitoring food intake through various technologies and methods, generally using cutting-edge approaches to achieve the best possible results. Even so, many elderly people live in sparsely populated rural areas—in Spain, 28.1% of the elderly population resides in such areas—where social and economic conditions are fragile. Applying these techniques in these settings is essential to improving quality of life and may also help reduce healthcare costs. It is also particularly difficult because this population has very specific and strict requirements for the use and deployment of technology. In this Systematic Literature Review (SLR), we examine the main proposed technologies and techniques to determine whether they can be used in this context and whether they can improve the quality of life of this vulnerable group. The review covers 326 papers, of which 29 proposals were fully analyzed, considering the characteristics and needs of this population.
